reviews.text: My cat injured his paw on August 10, 2026. I took him to the Lancer Clinic and saw a very kind young vet who explained that the wound was deep but not very well positioned, so we couldn't use stitches. She sedated my cat to provide initial treatment, and I had to apply dressings with a healing cream for a good week. We scheduled another appointment for about ten days later, on August 21, 2026, for a follow-up. I was already surprised to have to pay for a follow-up consultation, but no problem. I saw the doctor, who was anything but kind—a very cold man. No problem as long as he treated my cat. Imagine my surprise when this man told me he was going to sedate my cat again to put in stitches. So there I was, with a total bill of €300 for both visits. I picked up my cat the same day. This kind gentleman explained that the stitches were dissolvable and that there was no need for a follow-up appointment. Here I am, more than a month after my last visit, and my cat's stitches still haven't dissolved on their own, which is, after all, the main purpose of dissolvable stitches. After contacting the clinic, I spoke to a very kind lady on the phone who told me that the stitches can take up to a month to dissolve. I told her that August 21st was more than a month ago, so I was starting to get a little worried. She suggested I make another appointment with the kind doctor. I asked her if it would be charged again, like the follow-up appointment in August. She replied that "normally," no, the visit wouldn't be charged and told me that if my cat cooperated, they would remove the stitches. I told her that my cat is fearful and that he was very likely to resist. I also asked if their goal was to sedate my cat for the third time in two months. She confirmed that yes, they would sedate him if he didn't cooperate. Therefore, I didn't make another appointment with Dr. Gentil; I prefer to spare my cat a third anesthesia in less than two months and go to a reputable clinic.

Very disappointing experience - Lack of diagnostic rigor
I consulted a vet about my kitten, whom I found a month ago. The vet administered vaccinations, treated for lice, and mentioned a "suspected ringworm" without being certain.
Three weeks later, my daughter and I developed patches on our bodies. The vet confirmed ringworm. Another vet then asked me why a Wood's lamp (blue light) hadn't been used during the first consultation to confirm or rule out the diagnosis.

Consequences:
Over €180 in additional veterinary fees (very expensive antifungal treatment)
Medical treatments for my daughter and me
Inability to get booster vaccinations on schedule
Contamination that could have been avoided with a proper diagnosis
When I returned to the clinic to cancel the booster vaccinations, I expressed my disappointment. No apology, no compensation despite the health and financial consequences for my family.
Ringworm is extremely contagious and takes a long time to treat. An accurate diagnosis at the first consultation would have prevented this situation. I do not recommend this establishment.

Upon arriving at reception, I was asked if it was for her annual vaccination (not at all). During the consultation, the vet repeated if it was for the vaccination, I replied no and explained the situation. She then grimaced and simply glanced over, telling me that everything should be fine if she was on antibiotics, and rushed to administer the vaccination I had never requested (I know it's not the most pleasant thing to do, but that's why I came). They carefully preserved Praline's leash and harness in a lovely box, and included her four paw prints, which they then inked onto two cards: one for my brother and one for me. Today, we also received a letter of condolence from them.

Beyond their professionalism and the excellent care they provide to animals, we were deeply touched by their humanity, their attentiveness, and their empathy.
We wholeheartedly recommend this clinic.
